title: Dilli Haat Delhi - Shopping, Food, Culture & Travel Guide
content:
Dilli Haat - Delhi,

Dilli Haat is one of Delhi’s most vibrant shopping and cultural destinations. Unlike regular markets, it is designed like a traditional village haat (bazaar), showcasing India’s rich heritage. From handicrafts to handlooms, and from regional delicacies to cultural performances, Dilli Haat is a unique place where tradition meets modern shopping.

History & Overview:

Opened in 1994 at INA, and later expanded to Pitampura and Janakpuri, Dilli Haat was created to provide a platform for local artisans and craftsmen from across India. It gives visitors a chance to experience the diverse culture of India in one place – through art, craft, food, and music.

What Makes It Special:

Dilli Haat is not just a market, it’s an experience of India’s culture and lifestyle. You’ll find handmade jewelry, traditional textiles, paintings, wooden crafts, pottery, and home décor items. Each week, artisans from different states set up stalls, so the collection keeps changing. Adding to this charm, the open-air design, cultural performances, and folk dances make it even more special.

Things to Shop For:

  • Handcrafted jewelry and accessories.
  • Traditional Indian sarees, kurtas, and shawls.
  • Home décor items and wooden crafts.
  • Pottery, paintings, and souvenirs.
  • Organic and natural products.

Food & Eateries:

One of the biggest attractions of Dilli Haat is its food stalls representing different states of India. From Rajasthani dal baati churma to Momos from Nagaland, and from South Indian dosas to North Indian chole bhature, this place is a food lover’s paradise.

Entry Fee & Timings:

  • Entry Fee: ₹30 (Adults), ₹20 (Children), ₹100 (Foreigners).
  • Timings: Open daily, from 10:30 AM to 10:00 PM.

Best Time to Visit: Dilli Haat can be visited year-round, but the best time is October to March, when the weather is pleasant for walking around and enjoying the open-air market.

How to Reach:

  • Nearest Metro Station: INA Metro Station (for INA Dilli Haat), Netaji Subhash Place Metro Station (for Pitampura).
  • By Road: Easily accessible by auto, cab, or bus.
  • Parking: Both INA and Pitampura Dilli Haat have paid parking facilities available.

Places to Visit Nearby:

  • INA Dilli Haat: Safdarjung Tomb, Lodhi Garden, Sarojini Nagar Market.
  • Pitampura Dilli Haat: Japanese Park, Metro Walk Mall, Adventure Island.

Travel Tips:

  • Bargaining is limited, as prices are usually fixed.
  • Carry cash, although most stalls now accept UPI/digital payments.
  • Visit during weekends for cultural programs and performances.
  • Perfect place to buy souvenirs and gifts from Delhi.
excerpt: Dilli Haat (INA & Pitampura) is a cultural shopping paradise where you can experience India’s rich heritage through crafts, food, and performances. With its vibrant atmosphere and unique shopping options, it’s a must-visit for anyone looking to explore the cultural side of Delhi.

faqs.question: What is Dilli Haat famous for?
faqs.answer: Dilli Haat is famous for its handicrafts, handlooms, food stalls, and cultural events representing different states of India.

faqs.question: Which is better - Dilli Haat INA or Pitampura?
faqs.answer: Both are good, but INA Dilli Haat is more popular and centrally located, while Pitampura is spacious and less crowded.

faqs.question: What are Dilli Haat timings?
faqs.answer: Dilli Haat is open daily from 10:30 AM to 10:00 PM.

faqs.question: Can we try food from different states in Dilli Haat?
faqs.answer: Yes, Dilli Haat is known for its state-wise food stalls, offering authentic regional cuisines.

faqs.question: How many Dilli Haats are there in Delhi?
faqs.answer: There are three - INA, Pitampura, and Janakpuri.
